clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female presented with a 4-day painless lump in the posterior right thigh. Initial radiographs revealed a calcified mass in the posteromedial soft tissues with ill-defined central calcification. Targeted ultrasound demonstrated a hypoechoic mass with dense calcification and significant posterior acoustic shadowing. MRI characterized a 6.1 × 9.6 × 9.8 cm heterogeneously enhancing mass with infiltrative margins. The diagnosis of ESOS was favored based on imaging findings and confirmed via tissue sampling performed under Orthopedic guidance. CT staging showed absence of metastatic disease in the chest, abdomen, and pelvis. The case was discussed at the Sarcoma Multidisciplinary Tumor Board, and the patient was started on first-line chemotherapy with ifosfamide and etoposide. After the second cycle, she developed severe toxicity including confusion, pancytopenia, and atrial fibrillation requiring hospitalization, IV antibiotics, pegfilgrastim, and dabigatran. At 6-month follow-up, disease progression was noted; however, second-line systemic therapy was deemed high-risk due to recent atrial fibrillation and neutropenic sepsis, compounded by limited ambulation. Palliative radiation therapy (5 fractions) was elected for pain control alongside physiotherapy to improve mobility.
